top.title: Liverpool told to pay €40m to sign defender in January
top.description: Liverpool told to pay €40m to sign defender in January Liverpool tracking Ismaelo Ganiou as AC Milan circle €40m Lens defender Liverpool’s recruitment team appear to be casting the net widely ahead of the January window, with France once again emerging as a fertile market for young talent. Credit to Gazzetta Dello Sport, which reports that RC Lens defender Ismaelo Ganiou is attracting serious attention, with AC Milan also firmly in the picture and a fee of around €40m seemingly enough to strike a deal. From Liverpool’s side, the logic is easy to follow. The club has already leaned into the French market in recent windows and there is a growing sense that more business from that pipeline could follow. Ganiou, 21, is understood to be admired for his versatility, with the ability to operate at centre-back and right-back particularly appealing to clubs seeking depth without compromising tactical flexibility. French market remains central to Liverpool plans There is a broader pattern developing around Liverpool’s scouting in France. A number of names have already surfaced, particularly in midfield and defence, and the profile is familiar, young, high-upside footballers with room to develop and potential resale strength. Lamine Camara has been mentioned as one of the midfield options under consideration, while Arthur Avom and Mahamadou Nagida are also part of the wider picture. That does not automatically mean deals are close across the board. As ever, admiration and active negotiations are different stages entirely. Yet the volume of reporting around Ligue 1 talents does indicate where much of Liverpool’s attention currently lies. Why Ganiou fits Liverpool recruitment model Ganiou looks like the kind of player modern recruitment departments value highly. He is young, tactically aware and sufficiently composed in possession to contribute to build-up play. Those traits matter even more for a side that expects defenders to be comfortable defending space and progressing the ball under pressure. The reported €40m valuation will naturally shape the conversation. For a 21-year-old defender still building his reputation, it is a meaningful fee. Equally, in the current market, a player capable of covering multiple positions and growing within an elite environment can quickly look like sound value. Photo IMAGO AC Milan interest could test Liverpool resolve Milan’s presence in the race is worth noting. When a club of that stature is prepared to engage, the market can move quickly. Liverpool may admire the player, but timing, squad priorities and the final structure of any package would all influence whether interest becomes something more concrete. For now, this feels like a situation to monitor closely. Liverpool are clearly active in France, and Ganiou is another name placed prominently on that list. top.title: Bayern don't rule out Musiala sale as Rummenigge escalates dilemma
top.description: Bayern Munich's Jamal Musiala sits on the bench prior to the start of the German Bundesliga soccer match between Bayern Munich and 1. FC Cologne at Allianz Arena. (is associated with: «Bayern don't rule out Musiala sale as Rummenigge escalates dilemma») Tom Weller/dpa Bayern Munich are not ruling out the sale of Jamal Musiala as fresh statements from supervisory board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge have escalated the situation surrounding the midfielder. Musiala has been struggling with fitness since a serious injury at last year's Club World Cup, which forced him to miss half of the 2025-26 season. He made his comeback from yet another injury in Bayern's 1-1 draw with Cologne in the Bundesliga on Friday evening. However, there are concerns over his health after he collapsed earlier this year during two pre-season games. He later went public about a neurological condition. "He has a health-related issue. It's also well known that he has a contract involving very substantial sums of money. As a club, we have to consider how to deal with that situation. I think that's responsible and perfectly normal," Rummenigge said after the draw with Cologne. He said that selling the player "it's not out of the question. We suspect it will be difficult for him to get back to his previous level." However, Rummenigge added that he can't imagine another club would buy Musiala "under these circumstances. We have to think about the financial implications." Bayern honorary president Uli Hoeness recently has also expressed doubts whether Musiala would ever return to his previous level of play. "He has an illness that is not easily curable, but can be controlled to some extent with medication. But whether he will ever again have the performance level he once had..." "But now he is still getting paid. Just imagine if Bayern were now to question his contract and say: what he can now deliver is no longer what was in the contract," he said referring to Musiala's deal until 2030. Hoeness was criticized for his statements, but Rummenigge backed the remarks. "Uli's wording was correct. Very serious and fair. We have an interest in seeing him return and play well. If that doesn't happen, then we will have to think about the situation," he said.

top.title: Elliot Anderson scores but Man City frustrated by Fulham
top.description: Manchester City's Erling Haaland reacts during the English Premier League soccer match between Manchester City and Fulham at the Etihad Stadium. (is associated with: «Elliot Anderson scores but Man City frustrated by Fulham») Martin Rickett/PA Wire/dpa Elliot Anderson struck as Manchester City ended their losing run but more points were dropped as Fulham claimed a 1-1 draw at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday. After Erling Haaland had an equalizer controversially disallowed, England midfielder Anderson netted with a sweet volley just before the hour to cancel out Rodrigo Muniz’s well-crafted opener. It was enough to end City’s run of three successive Premier League defeats but left them without a win in the competition for five weeks after opening the campaign with seven wins in a row. The main talking point was Haaland’s disallowed goal after 25 minutes, when the Norwegian prodded home from close range after a fumble by Fulham goalkeeper Bernd Leno. To City’s frustration, the German was deemed to still be in control of the ball. The draw ended Fulham’s run of 20 consecutive defeats against City in all competitions and continued their recent upturn in form under Alvaro Arbeloa, with the Cottagers now unbeaten in five Premier League games.

top.title: 3 keys to a Jets win at the Chargers in Week 11
top.description: The New York Jets and Los Angeles Chargers enter Week 11 with a lot on the line. That's probably strange to say for two teams with a combined 16 losses through the first 11 weeks of the NFL season. In total, they have met 39 times, with the first meeting coming in 1960. That includes two postseason clashes. New York won both playoff meetings, but the Chargers hold a 24-14-1 advantage in the all-time series, with the tie coming in 1964. It's been a long time since the Jets won, dropping five straight in the series. Their last victory came in 2011, while the most recent meeting ended in a loss in 2023. This seems like an opportunity for New York to finally take one, but head coach Aaron Glenn's squad has taught us that nothing with this team is guaranteed. Still, expect Jets fans to find their way in front of a television anyway. The Jets (2-8) need more than a few promising stretches to finally put a game away. If they want to leave Los Angeles (1-8) with a victory. Here are Jets Wire's five keys to pulling off a win against the Chargers: Jets must take advantage of a team playing on a short week The Chargers have the advantage of playing at home, but they also have considerably less time to recover and prepare after Monday night's road victory. A short week can take a toll, particularly on a defense that must repeatedly defend long drives and deal with the physical demands of stopping the run. This is where the Jets could find an advantage. Establishing the rushing attack, moving the chains, and forcing Los Angeles' defense to spend more time on the field would help New York control the tempo. The Chargers have struggled when allowing explosive plays, and the Jets need to take advantage of that vulnerability rather than abandoning the ground game when opportunities are there. Keeping the offense ahead of the chains would also make life easier for whoever starts at quarterback. The Jets don't need to turn this into a shootout. They need to make the Chargers work for every possession while taking advantage of a defense playing on short rest. Stabilizing quarterback play Geno Smith left Sunday's loss to the Buffalo Bills with an ankle injury after previously being evaluated for a concussion. That opened the door for Cade Klubnik, who completed 11 of 20 passes for 137 yards, but he was sacked three times and threw an interception. Smith seems set to return against Los Angeles, but his availability remains uncertain. Regardless of who gets the start, the Jets need a more stable performance under center. That means protecting the football, avoiding unnecessary pressure and giving the offense opportunities to stay on the field. The red-zone issues also have to improve. top.title: 3 keys to a Bills win vs. the Dolphins in Week 11
top.description: The Buffalo Bills are looking to stay in the win column in Week 11 as they head back home to take on the Miami Dolphins at Highmark Stadium. The Bills (8-1) have won their last five games and are trying to keep the momentum going. How can Buffalo get the upper hand against the Dolphins (1-8)? Here are Bills Wire's three keys to victory in Week 11: Efficient passing Last week against the New York Jets, Josh Allen completed just 52.4% of his passes (11-for-21), recorded a passer rating of 80.7, and threw an interception. While Allen scored twice with his legs and the Bills ran away with the game, it wasn't an efficient game from him. This week, he'll have a chance to bounce back against another divisional rival. This year, the Dolphins are allowing the highest completion percentage for opposing quarterbacks in the NFL (73.7%). Allen and the passing game have a chance to get right at an important part of the season. Work the ground game James Cook continues to be the workhorse for the Bills offense, having at least 18 carries in seven of the last eight games for Buffalo. Last week, he ran for 157 yards and a touchdown, including a 74-yard house call to put the Jets to bed. The Dolphins have struggled on defense this year. They have the 27th-ranked run defense according to DVOA. The Bills should look to take control of this one and pound the rock. Perhaps they'll look to involve Ray Davis more out of the backfield in this one with a short week coming up for the Chiefs Thanksgiving matchup. Keep beating up on backup QBs The Bills defense has caught a break recently. Over their last three games, the've faced a backup QB in every matchup due to injury. In Week 8, they faced both Tyley Huntley and Joe Fagnano of the Ravens after Lamar Jackson went down. In Week 9 against the Vikings, they faced Carson Wentz. And, in Week 10, Geno Smith exited and they faced rookie Cade Clubnik. The Bills defense has stepped up in a major way the past three weeks after a rocky start to the season. They didn't allow a single touchdown in all three games. But, how much of it is from facing low-level offenses and how much should be credited to the defense for turning things around? It is more of the same for the Bills this week as they'll get Dolphins rookie QB Kyle McCord out of Syracuse after Malik Willis was put on IR . top.title: Haaland in VAR controversy as Man City held by Fulham
top.description: Erling Haaland was controversially denied a crucial goal as Manchester City’s spluttering Premier League title challenge suffered a fresh blow in a 1-1 draw against Fulham on Saturday. Enzo Maresca’s side trailed to Rodrigo Muniz’s early opener at the Etihad Stadium before Haaland’s equaliser was contentiously ruled out. The City striker kicked the ball out of the grasp of Fulham keeper Bernd Leno on the goal-line. But Leno barely had two hands on the ball when Haaland made contact, giving City reason to feel aggrieved with the decision. Elliot Anderson saved City from a fourth successive league defeat as the England midfielder equalised in the second half with his first top-flight goal since signing from Nottingham Forest in the close-season. But it was another frustrating afternoon for third-placed City, who could not find a winner and were booed off at full-time. Leaders Arsenal can extend their lead over City to eight points if they win at Newcastle later on Saturday. After making a blistering start to the season with seven successive league wins, City are winless in their last four top-flight matches. It was the first time in 15 years and 21 games that City had failed to beat Fulham. Still waiting to discover the result of their appeal against the guilty verdict over breaches of Premier League financial rules, City have looked increasingly distracted in recent weeks. Maresca has claimed City are not bothered by the “noise” around the financial scandal, which is likely to include a huge points deduction if the appeal fails. But his team’s lethargic performances of late suggest otherwise, with tricky tests against Napoli on Tuesday and Arsenal next weekend threatening to extend their slump. – Slumping City – City needed a fast start to ease their anxiety and Erling Haaland almost delivered it when his looping header was cleared off the line. But Maresca has failed to fix the defensive problems that ailed City in their previous three games. Fulham took full advantage of City’s flaws to snatch the lead with an incisive counter in the 16th minute. Former City winger Oscar Bobb pounced on a wayward pass and accelerated down the right flank before picking out Muniz’s run into the penalty area. With City’s defence in disarray, Muniz kept his composure to curl a fine finish into the top corner. Maresca turned away in disgust and his frustration only increased when City were denied a leveller in the 26th minute. Iliman Ndiaye’s cross reached Haaland inside the six-yard box but the Norway striker’s weak volley was saved by Leno. Haaland’s momentum carried him into Leno and he kicked the ball over the line as the Fulham keeper struggled to get hold of it. But Haaland’s celebrations were curtailed by VAR’s decision to disallow the goal for a foul on Leno. top.description: Wendell Cruz-Imagn Images. Mets rumors: Mark Vientos emerges as trade candidate, but there’s a catch appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Mets have received trade interest in Mark Vientos , but a deal does not appear imminent. The Mets tendered the first baseman and designated hitter a contract for 2027 on Friday, keeping him under club control. New York tendered Vientos before Friday’s 5 p.m. ET deadline. The 26-year-old is eligible for salary arbitration for the first time this offseason. The Mets can still trade him while they weigh their options at first base and designated hitter. Vientos hit 27 home runs during his 2024 breakout and carried that power into the postseason. His production declined over the next two seasons, leaving his role in Queens less certain heading into 2027. A fractured right hand limited his playing time, though he posted an .809 OPS vs. left-handed pitching. The Mets also have Jorge Polanco and Jared Young as options at first base and designated hitter. Injuries limited Polanco to 37 games in 2026. Polanco remains under contract for 2027, so the club already has a veteran alternative. Young gives New York a left-handed hitter who can fill either spot. Vientos is out of minor league options, which limits how the Mets can manage their roster. They would have to expose him to waivers before sending him to the minors. The tender keeps him in the organization while New York evaluates its lineup. After a brutal 2026 season, the Mets wants to right the ship in 2027. If Vientos stays in Queens, his success against left-handed pitching gives New York a clear way to use his bat. top.title: Berrada insists Manchester United signings made squad 'fundamentally better' despite relegation fight
top.description: Berrada insists Manchester United signings made squad 'fundamentally better' despite relegation fight Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada has insisted the club's recent signings have made the squad 'fundamentally better', even with United sitting 18th in the Premier League table . Berrada sat down Sky Sports to discuss the club's start to the season, the sacking of Michael Carrick and the criticism aimed at United's leadership. United dismissed Carrick during the November international break and appointed Mauricio Pochettino , whose first match in charge is away at Liverpool tomorrow. It is the third season in a row in which the club have changed head coach mid-campaign. Recruitment has been a particular flashpoint. Lisandro Martinez publicly criticised technical director Jason Wilcox for not preparing the team well enough in the transfer window, while Bruno Fernandes took aim at the methods of Carrick and his coaching staff. 'We will not spend just for the sake of it' Berrada nonetheless defended United's business. He named Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans, Santos, Karl Darlow and returning loanee Marcus Rashford as additions that had improved the group. "In our view Baleba, Tielemans, Santos and Karl Darlow, as well as Marcus Rashford, have made the squad fundamentally better."When we find the right opportunity, we will spend money. But again, we won't spend for the sake of it." - Omar Berrada 'I am convinced that we are heading in the right direction' United finished third in the Premier League last season to secure Champions League football, but are in the relegation places after 10 games in 2026/27. Despite that, Berrada said he was confident the club were heading in the right direction. "100%. I know it's difficult to say this when you're sitting 18th in the Premier League table. It's clear - it's not good enough, not acceptable, and that's why we've made the change that we've made, so that we can move forward. top.title: Browns roster: 2 backups who could help take the offense to another level
top.description: Fans of the Cleveland Browns are enjoying a peaceful bye week before preparing for Week 12’s Sunday Night Football matchup with the Las Vegas Raiders . There are still a ton of questions surrounding the Browns, including whether they are actually a good team or just happened to win games . Cleveland HC Todd Monken must use the bye week to get the team’s running game going and figure out how to help in the early part of the game . Beyond that, the offense has to find more stabilit y, much of which could come through the rushing attack and a schedule with defenses that can be attacked . While many will point to the offensive line, QB Deshaun Watson , and RB Quinshon Judkins as places where the Browns offense needs to improve, two backups could help take the offense to another level: RB Dylan Sampson and WR Isaiah Bond . Now, neither player is likely to take over significantly more snaps for the rest of the season, although Bond needs a few more if he’s going to make any impact at all, but both have a chance to help Monken’s offense be more explosive in different ways. Sampson is not just a change-of-pace back, but one who can make big plays in ways that Judkins just can’t. Misdirection runs, screen plays, dump-off passes, and the occasional late leak-out play could all give Watson and company big gains and keep the offense on the field. Sampson’s ability to make plays all over the field and from a variety of positions makes him a versatile threat that must be accounted for. Bond, on the other hand, has really one gift to give the Browns offense: straight-line speed. Unfortunately, mistimed jumps and drops have led Monken to limit the speedster’s snaps in favor of veterans Malachi Corley and Tylan Wallace . If Monken can trust the second-year receiver and he makes just a couple of big plays in the first few games coming out of the bye week, Bond can not only become impactful in the stat sheet but also as a decoy. Having Bond run deep post, 9-route, and corner routes can take the top off of a defense, pull the safety away, and create more spacing underneath for all of the above-mentioned players, along with TE Harold Fannin Jr. , to make plays after the catch. top.title: 2027: Tinubu takes swipe at Makinde, urges Oyo voters to choose APC
top.description: By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja President Bola Tinubu has told the people of Oyo State not to mind Governor Seyi Makinde, the presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), and urged them to vote for the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) from top to bottom. The president spoke on Saturday at the APC presidential rally in Ibadan, the Oyo state capital. Apparently referring to the governor, the president said, “There is a party out there parading themselves. Please don’t mind them and don’t listen to them. They are only interested in clearing what you have. Vote for APC from top to bottom.” Tinubu said he would not speak at length. “I will not be able to speak much to you. I just want to greet you. This is our party. It is your party. Is that clear? “You voted overwhelmingly for the APC last time. You must stay the course for the sake of progress, the prosperity of our country and the development of your children and great-grandchildren,” he said. Before addressing the rally, the president asked the gathering to observe a minute of silence for the victims of the boat accident in Bayelsa State. “Our condolences go to the people of Bayelsa State and the bereaved families. May God grant the people of Bayelsa peace and happiness and prevent a recurrence of such an incident. We will support them,” he said. Tinubu also announced an investment for Oyo State. “For your state, we have just signed an agreement with China’s Yutong to reopen the old Leyland factory in Ibadan. top.title: AWS got hit by an outage too. Here's why you didn't hear about it
top.description: My editor asked me this week "why is everything except AWS breaking?" It's a great question! They haven't been in the headlines! In fact, as they are wont to do, AWS spokesperson Patrick Neighorn g ot salty to a reporter about how unreliable Downdetector is when it started showing them as impacted. If you'll permit me a small digression, this stems from a misunderstanding of what Downdetector is for. Historically the AWS status site was so hilariously slow to reflect the lived customer experience that some jackass (me) built a rewriter that sits at stop.lying.cloud to make it a smidgen more realistic. As a result, the question people are really trying to answer when they visit Downdetector is "my app just broke; is it my crappy code or is there a global event going on?" There are mitigations for both, but they look nothing alike. AWS view crowdsourced reports of the form "the internet is broken, must be AWS" as a stain upon their honor. In fact, it's a badge of their own success, as "the internet" and "AWS" have become inextricably linked in people's minds. But back to my editor's question, "why didn't AWS go down?" Easy: it did. Everything breaks, all the time, including the narrative AWS now has 34 generally available commercial regions, of which two are currently smoking craters due to the Iran conflict. Each of these has hundreds of services that AWS offers to customers, of which a dozen or so are high quality, if I'm being characteristically uncharitable. They experience degradation in various ways, and they go largely unnoticed. But on November 15, AWS confirmed an incident that disrupted 11 of those ~12 good services in their oldest and most important region, us-east-1. At 3:05 AM PST, they stated that they started seeing sign-up errors, authentication issues, and connectivity issues. Five minutes later engineers were engaged. Not to be outdone, their status page swung into action after a leisurely coffee, and posted its first indication of an incident 93 minutes later. (See previous comments on stop.lying.cloud ). The all-clear showed up at 6:53 AM. Every site has downtime. Sometimes it blows up publicly, other times nobody seems to notice. Heck, AWS said in September that it had experienced permanent data loss in its two smoking craters, but after that news cycle passed I haven't heard a thing about it. I do think it's patently unreasonable to blame them for this specific problem; "acts of war" are kinda hard to predict from the corporate planning meeting. nigeria.description: Erling Haaland was controversially denied a crucial goal as Manchester City’s spluttering Premier League title challenge suffered a fresh blow in a 1-1 draw against Fulham on Saturday. The City striker kicked the ball out of the grasp of Fulham keeper Bernd Leno on the goal-line. But Leno barely had two hands on the ball when Haaland made contact, giving City reason to feel aggrieved with the decision. Elliot Anderson saved City from a fourth successive league defeat as the England midfielder equalised in the second half with his first top-flight goal since signing from Nottingham Forest in the close-season. But it was another frustrating afternoon for third-placed City, who could not find a winner and were booed off at full-time. Leaders Arsenal can extend their lead over City to eight points if they win at Newcastle later on Saturday. After making a blistering start to the season with seven successive league wins, City are winless in their last four top-flight matches. It was the first time in 15 years and 21 games that City had failed to beat Fulham. Still waiting to discover the result of their appeal against the guilty verdict over breaches of Premier League financial rules, City have looked increasingly distracted in recent weeks. Maresca has claimed City are not bothered by the “noise” around the financial scandal, which is likely to include a huge points deduction if the appeal fails. The president spoke on Saturday at the APC presidential rally in Ibadan, the Oyo state capital. Apparently referring to the governor, the president said, “There is a party out there parading themselves. Please don’t mind them and don’t listen to them. They are only interested in clearing what you have. Vote for APC from top to bottom.” Tinubu said he would not speak at length. “I will not be able to speak much to you. I just want to greet you. This is our party. It is your party. Is that clear? “You voted overwhelmingly for the APC last time. You must stay the course for the sake of progress, the prosperity of our country and the development of your children and great-grandchildren,” he said. Before addressing the rally, the president asked the gathering to observe a minute of silence for the victims of the boat accident in Bayelsa State. “Our condolences go to the people of Bayelsa State and the bereaved families. May God grant the people of Bayelsa peace and happiness and prevent a recurrence of such an incident. We will support them,” he said. Tinubu also announced an investment for Oyo State. “For your state, we have just signed an agreement with China’s Yutong to reopen the old Leyland factory in Ibadan. We are reopening it to produce public transport vehicles and establish an automobile assembly plant there. We will continue to bring industries. You will see progress and development,” he added. Speaking on behalf of the APC governors, the governor of Ekiti State, Mr Biodun Oyebanji, urged the Yoruba to turn out for the President. “We are appealing to the Yoruba people, particularly our sons and daughters, to come out and support the presidential candidate, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. On January 16, let us all come out and vote for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and Senator Sarafadeen Ali of the APC. When the time comes, we will also support our candidates contesting for the Senate, House of Representatives and State House of Assembly. “I appeal to the Yoruba people not to allow this opportunity to slip away. Let us stand together and ensure that our party succeeds in Nigeria,” Oyebanji said. The post 2027: Tinubu takes swipe at Makinde, urges Oyo voters to choose APC appeared first on Vanguard News .

nigeria.title: Diallo present as African football boss Motsepe reiterates support for Infantino
nigeria.description: African football supremo Patrice Motsepe said Saturday that all 54 members of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) support Gianni Infantino’s bid for re-election as FIFA president. Motsepe made the declaration in Abuja, where CAF is holding its ordinary general assembly and at which one of Infantino’s two rivals, French football chief Philippe Diallo is present. Former Japan Football Association president Kozo Tashima is the other candidate. The trio will learn whether they have been successful on March 18 next year in Rabat — the winning candidate must obtain a majority of the 211 associations. CAF’s support for Infantino comes hours after another of his steadfast supporters South American football’s governing body CONMEBOL gave him their “unanimous” backing. CAF has been consistently behind Infantino — who is seeking a fourth and final term — even after the furore he stirred up in July with his shortlived FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors. Morocco is co-hosting the 2030 World Cup. “Gianni, you have our support on behalf of the 54 nations in Africa to be our candidate,” Motsepe said. “I have a report from all 54 member associations in Africa to say that we are unanimously supporting Gianni.” Infantino has faced multiple calls to step down and lost the backing of European football’s governing body UEFA, whilst CONCACAF has also been strident in its criticism of the 56-year-old Swiss lawyer. Motsepe though has been a vocal supporter and Infantino said such loyalty was reciprocal. “You will always find, in me and in FIFA, a trusted partner,” Infantino told the assembly, announcing cash inflow of $25 million to each member of CAF, starting January 2027 for development projects. On Wednesday, UEFA vice-president Laura McAllister told AFP that Diallo, a 63-year-old lawyer whose Senegalese-born father boxed for France at the 1960 Olympics in Rome, should not be seen as solely a European candidate. “He is a francophone, which is an important asset in lots of CAF countries,” she said. McAllister, who in 2023 became the first woman to be elected a vice-president of UEFA, noted though that confederations do not vote as a bloc. “There is a soft space which Philippe can exploit and convince some federations within each confederation to support a reform agenda,” the 61-year-old said. “There is a lot of discomfort around the behaviour of Gianni Infantino and a desire to challenge the concentration of power in his hands. “This applies everywhere in world football. This is not about Europe, the same rules apply globally.” The post Diallo present as African football boss Motsepe reiterates support for Infantino appeared first on Vanguard News .

nigeria.title: Tinubu inaugurates UI medical hostel, promises 50,000 bed spaces in federal varsities
nigeria.description: President Bola Tinubu has pledged to deliver additional 50,000 bed space hostels across federal tertiary institutions by the end of 2027 to tackle accommodation challenges confronting students Tinubu made the pledge on Saturday at the inauguration of Block E of the College of Medicine hostel, University of Ibadan (UI), located at Alexander Brown Hall, University College Hospital. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the hostel block was donated by the Chagoury family. The President, represented by the Minister of Education, Dr Maruf Alausa, said that the 50,000 bed space hostels would be delivered through the ₦400 billion Student Hostels Programme, implemented via the Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund) and Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs). He said the initiative was aimed at providing students with safe and decent accommodation to support their education. “The accommodation shortage at the College of Medicine has become a critical challenge following the 2020 directive of the Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria (MDCN) requiring clinical students of medicine and dentistry to reside within the University College Hospital (UCH) premises for accreditation purposes. “The college faced a shortfall of 490 bed spaces, representing 44.5 per cent of its accommodation requirement, leaving many students exposed to insecurity and difficulties attending essential clinical sessions,” the president said. According to him, the shortage also prevented the college from fully utilising its annual admission quota for the Bachelor of Medicine, Bachelor of Surgery (MBBS) programme. Tinubu said his administration was prioritising education funding and reforms through initiatives such as the Nigerian Education Sector Renewal Initiative, Nigeria Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), TETFund and the Student Venture Capital Grant. He added that more than 36 universities had benefited from the Renewed Hope Energising Education Programme, with power installations ranging from 2.5 megawatts to 12 megawatts. The President also said that the government had completed 20 compressed natural gas (CNG) conversion centres and maintenance facilities in some universities, with 40 additional facilities expected by the end of 2028. Earlier, the Vice-Chancellor of UI, Prof. Peter Olapegba, said the inauguration of Block E marked another milestone in efforts to provide adequate accommodation for medical students and meet accreditation requirements. Olapegba expressed appreciation to the benefactors, Ambassador Gilbert Ramez Chagoury and his brother, Ronald Chagoury, for their contribution to medical education. “The hostel, named the Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu GCFR Block, provides accommodation for 192 medical and dental students in 48 rooms, with four students per room. “The building also has four reading rooms, each measuring about 71 square metres, as well as rooms equipped with toilets, showers and kitchenettes,” Olapegba said. nigeria.title: Mexico captures drug kingpin on FBI’s most wanted list
nigeria.description: Mexico’s military announced on Saturday that it had captured the leader of a drug-trafficking group who was among the 10 most-wanted fugitives sought by US law enforcement. Fausto Isidro Meza, alias “Chapo Isidro,” and two other leaders of his drug gang were captured during a special forces raid Friday night in Sinaloa state, the Mexican National Defense Secretariat announced on X. A firefight ensued between the military and gang members in the town of Guasave, sparking panic in the surrounding area, including at a professional baseball game, local media reported. “Chapo Isidro” is the alleged leader of the Beltran Leyva gang, which is allied with one of two rival factions in the powerful Sinaloa cartel, Mexico’s military said. He was captured alongside his number two in the group and another man identified as a financial operator. They were all transported by a Mexican Air Force aircraft to Mexico City “to be placed at the disposal of the competent prosecutorial authorities,” the military said. Chapo Isidro faces criminal charges in both Mexico and the United States. The FBI had placed him on its list of 10 most wanted fugitives and offered a $5 million reward for information leading to his arrest. Giving his name as Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores, the FBI bulletin says his group is responsible for importing “large quantities of heroin, methamphetamine, cocaine, fentanyl, and marijuana into the United States.” The post Mexico captures drug kingpin on FBI’s most wanted list appeared first on Vanguard News .

nigeria.title: FG increases medical student admission to 12,000, targets 20,000 annually — Alausa
nigeria.description: The Federal Government has increased annual admission into medical schools from 5,000 to 12,000 students, the Minister of Education, Dr. Tunji Alausa, has said. Alausa, who stated this on the sidelines of the inauguration of a 192-bed hostel at the College of Medicine, University of Ibadan (UI), on Saturday, said that it targets enrollment of 20,000 students annually. The minister said the increase in enrollment was part of efforts to address manpower shortages in the health sector amid the migration of Nigerian medical professionals abroad. He said that the government, since President Bola Tinubu assumed office, had increased nursing enrollment from about 28,000 annually to more than 130,000. According to him, the country is making progress in producing more healthcare professionals. Alausa, who represented Tinubu at the inauguration, said the administration was investing in infrastructure to expand the capacity of medical schools and other tertiary institutions to accommodate more students. According to him, annual admission into medical schools has risen to about 12,000, from 5,000 students recorded before the administration began in May 2023. “We decided that in four years, we will increase the number to 20,000 annually. “Three years into it, we are enrolling about 12,000 medical students now across all our medical schools in the country, and by the end of 2028, we will meet our target of enrolling over 20,000 medical students,” he said. Alausa said the government had also increased admission into dentistry, pharmacy, physiotherapy, and other allied health programs to strengthen the country’s healthcare workforce. He said the expansion was being complemented by investments in infrastructure, including hostels, to support increased enrollment and improve the learning environment. The minister added that the government was also investing in the education sector through the Nigeria Education Sector Renewal Initiative. “This includes the construction and rehabilitation of schools, expansion of medical schools, and re-equipping of engineering workshops,” the minister said. Alausa said the administration had invested nearly N500 billion in educational infrastructure, adding that the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) had also expanded access to tertiary education for students irrespective of their economic backgrounds. He urged journalists to verify the figures on nursing and medical student enrollment through the relevant regulatory bodies, including the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria. nigeria.title: The Governor, The Candidate And The Voter
nigeria.description: Anambra puts the power of endorsements to the test, while opposition negotiations and election safeguards face approaching deadlines. On Thursday in Awka, Governor Chukwuma Soludo presented APGA’s flag to Vice-President Kashim Shettima, who received it on behalf of President Bola Tinubu. On Friday, Peter Obi took his campaign through Onitsha, attracting supporters ahead of his town hall engagement. Two neighbouring cities offered competing pictures of political strength. In Awka, the message was partnership with the centre. In Onitsha, Obi demonstrated his continuing ability to mobilise in the state he once governed. The electoral question lies between those pictures: how far can a governor’s endorsement move presidential votes, and how effectively can a candidate convert personal loyalty into turnout? Anambra will help answer both. Soludo’s Wager APGA’s support gives Tinubu an organised partner outside the APC. Soludo is making an argument about the South-East’s place in national politics: that cooperation with the President offers a route to influence and development. The presentation reaffirmed APGA’s presidential alignment while the party continues pursuing its own interests in other elections. For Tinubu, the opportunity lies in improving his reach through a political organisation rooted in the state. For Soludo, the challenge is to persuade people who support his governorship to make the same choice in a presidential contest. Those loyalties need not coincide. Voters can approve of a governor’s performance and prefer another presidential candidate. They can also reconsider a previous choice if a new alliance offers a convincing case. The evidence will emerge through sustained mobilisation, local organisation and ultimately the ballot. A flag presentation establishes an endorsement. It cannot establish the electorate’s response. Obi’s Home-State Test Obi’s Onitsha road show supplies evidence of campaign activity and visible support. It does not, on its own, measure the balance of opinion across Anambra. His task is to maintain that support while building sufficient reach elsewhere. The home-state contest also brings his governing record into sharper focus. Obi has chosen to defend that record publicly; Soludo is advancing a different argument about Anambra’s political interests. Voters deserve an exchange grounded in verifiable achievements, present needs and credible proposals. Claims that cooperation necessarily delivers prosperity or that popular enthusiasm guarantees victory require testing. Anambra’s significance extends beyond its presidential tally. It offers a clear case study in the relationship between party machinery, a governor’s influence and a candidate’s personal following. nigeria.title: Nigeria endorses Infantino for another term as FIFA president
nigeria.description: Nigeria has declared its support for Gianni Infantino’s bid to retain the presidency of the world football governing body, FIFA, in the 2027 election. The Chairman of the National Sports Commission, Shehu Dikko, announced the Federal Government’s endorsement on Saturday during the 48th Ordinary General Assembly of the Confederation of African Football in Abuja. Speaking on behalf of President Bola Tinubu, Dikko said Nigeria would back Infantino’s re-election and called on other African football associations to support his continued leadership. “I must make it clear here on behalf of the Federal Government and in regard to the resolution of all the members of CAF that Nigeria firmly endorses Mr Gianni Infantino’s candidacy for the election. “This is a direct message that was given to us by the President and Commander-in-Chief of the Federal Republic of Nigeria,” he said. “We recognise Mr Gianni’s contribution to the advancement of football worldwide, particularly in Africa, and urge our fellow African member associations to stand firmly together in support of his continued leadership. “This is in our collective interest,” he added. The NSC chairman also praised Infantino’s administration, drawing on his experience in football management to argue that the FIFA president’s decisions had served the interests of the sport. “Before I conclude, if I put my heart as a football person, Mr President, as a former member of the NFL Exco, Chairman of the League, member of the FIFA Seconders Committee, and founding member of the World League Forum, I must tell you, Gianni’s decisions are very, very good for football. They are very apt for football,” he said. He maintained that Infantino’s central responsibility was to grow the game and generate more revenue, arguing that disagreements within football administration largely concerned how the funds were shared. “His main job is to develop football and bring revenues to football. He tries to do that. The entire issue we are seeing across the world here today has nothing to do with bringing the revenues or the distribution. It’s all about distributing these revenues,” Dikko said. Nigeria’s declaration came at the same gathering where CAF president Patrice Motsepe reiterated the continental body’s backing for Infantino’s re-election. Infantino, who became FIFA president in 2016, is seeking another four-year term at the election scheduled to hold in Morocco in March 2027 with French Football Federation president Philippe Diallo and Japan Football Association honorary president Kozo Tashima set to challenge him. nigeria.title: ‘A fine gift to our generation’, Olajengbesi hails Davido on birthday
nigeria.description: Human rights lawyer, Pelumi Olajengbesi, has described Afrobeats star David Adeleke, popularly known as Davido, as one of the fine gifts to the present generation. In a Facebook post on Saturday to celebrate the singer’s birthday, Olajengbesi, who was the campaign spokesman for the re-election of Davido’s uncle, Governor Ademola Adeleke of Osun State, applauded the greatness of the Adeleke family. Olajengbesi said, “Happy Birthday Davido, thank you for who you are to everyone who meets you. You are one of the finest gifts to our generation. I am not just grateful to you and your family, I am indebted for life. “I have seen men, I have seen great families, but I have not seen many like the Adelekes. Blessed by God, graced by men, strengthened by love, bound together by service, and united by a generosity of spirit that transcends generations. “There is something extraordinary about a family whose greatness is measured not merely by wealth, influence or accomplishments, but by the number of lives they have touched, the doors they have opened and the hope they continue to inspire in others. “I pray that the Almighty God continues to preserve you, enlarge your coast, strengthen your home and grant you greater accomplishments. May your light never grow dim, and may generations yet unborn find inspiration in the legacy you are building.” Back in September, Davido endorsed the ambition of Olajengbesi to contest the Oriade-Obokun Federal Constituency seat in the 2027 general elections. Davido had described Olajengbesi as his next project following the governor’s victory at the poll. Olajengbesi is contesting against Wole Oke of the All Progressives Congress, who has occupied the seat for 24 years. The lawyer has garnered support from the likes of popular singer Dapo Oyebanjo, aka D’banj; Spotlite Nation boss Moses Bliss; and Yoruba Nation campaigner Sunday Igboho, among others. nigeria.title: Severe Storm Destroys Thousands Of Homes, Kills Three In Brazil
nigeria.description: A powerful storm with winds exceeding 100 kilometers per hour killed three people and destroyed around 5,000 homes Friday in southern Brazil, as authorities raced to rescue injured survivors and find more casualties in the wreckage. Rain and high winds battered Tupancireta early Friday, tearing up buildings and about 100 trees in the municipality that is home to 20,000 people. “It’s something never seen before, a movie scene,” Tupancireta Mayor Gustavo Herter told local media. “Our hospital was blocked by the trees around it, the access roads to the municipality were blocked with trees. The city is finished,” he said. The hospital’s roof was also destroyed and 11 patients had to be transferred. The city was without electricity and water after the storm hit at around 3 am and lasted less than an hour, Herter said. Three people were found dead, according to the state government of Rio Grande do Sul, where Tupancireta is located. Another 32 municipalities also reported damage. This handout picture released by Rio Grande do Sul Civil Defence Department shows the damage caused by strong winds in Tupancireta, Rio Grande do Sul state, Brazil, on November 20, 2026. President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva ordered emergency teams be sent to the region in response to the storm. “We know there was a party in the municipality where the roof of that structure ended up collapsing,” Luciano Boeira, state coordinator of civil defense, told Radio Gaucha. Brazilian meteorologists said winds reached 114 kilometers per hour (70 miles per hour) during the storm. Civil defense described the storm as a “supercell,” which often precedes a tornado with strong upward air currents, and has not ruled out the possibility that a tornado hit the city. State officials have allocated about $330,000 in local currency to respond to the disaster. Southern Brazil is frequently hit by tornadoes. nigeria.title: ‘I’ll be back’: vows Kane after ankle surgery
nigeria.description: Bayern Munich’s star striker Harry Kane pledged to return for the “business end of the season” after undergoing surgery on his left ankle on Saturday. Kane limped off after 20 minutes of Bayern’s 1-1 home draw with Cologne in their Bundesliga match on Friday, the club confirming the England captain had torn a ligament in his ankle. Bayern issued a statement Saturday saying the Ballon d’Or winner had “successfully undergone surgery” on his left ankle. “The 33-year-old will now begin his rehabilitation program,” Bayern said, with the injury expected to keep Kane out for three to four months. Kane posted a picture on social media from his hospital bed on Saturday, vowing to work his way back to fitness this season. “The highs and lows of life! Obviously very disappointed to get this injury but as always it’s an opportunity to show resilience and improvement going into 2027. “I’ll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season.” Kane shared a quote from three-time Super Bowl-winning wide receiver Julian Edelman: “tough times don’t last, tough people do”, while thanking his supporters for their messages of support. Kane has a history of ankle issues although he has only missed a handful of games since moving to Bayern in 2023. England coach Thomas Tuchel will be keeping a keen eye out on how England’s most capped player’s rehabilitation progresses. England play Norway in the Nations League quarter-finals in late March. The injury comes at a difficult time for Bayern, who are currently missing several players, particularly up front. Bayern are without Luis Diaz, Serge Gnabry, Alphonso Davies, Ismael Saibari and captain Manuel Neuer, while midfielder Jamal Musiala and coach Vincent Kompany both returned after long lay-offs on Friday. business.title: SEC Freezes Assets in $560 Million Crypto Trading Ponzi Scheme
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine SEC Freezes Assets in $560 Million Crypto Trading Ponzi Scheme The Securities and Exchange Commission has frozen the assets of Indianapolis-based Backward Hat Capital and its two co-founders, saying the firm ran a $560 million Ponzi scheme that told investors their money would be turned into crypto and used for AI-driven currency trading. The agency said Backward Hat, co-founders Phillip Williams and Devin Johnson, Johnson’s firm Traders Point Capital and Joseph Anderson raised the money from more than 2,000 investors starting in July 2022. A federal court granted a temporary restraining order, an asset freeze and expedited discovery to halt what the SEC called an ongoing scheme. Federal prosecutors in New York and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission brought parallel cases. The SEC and CFTC suits were filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Indiana, and the CFTC said the court has appointed Kevin B. Duff as temporary receiver to take control of the companies and the individual defendants’ assets. The pitch: crypto, AI and 6% a month According to the SEC’s complaint , Williams and Johnson sold limited partnership interests in private funds through a network of promoters, including to Williams’s former investment advisory clients. They promised a proprietary, “AI-driven” algorithm that supposedly returned at least 6% every month by trading foreign exchange. Investor money, the pitch went, would first be converted into a crypto asset and then used for that arbitrage. The complaint does not name bitcoin as the asset. It says about $109 million of the roughly $210 million raised from July 2022 to September 2025 was sent to the fund’s Coinbase account and converted. Of that, more than $56 million went to personal crypto accounts held by Williams, Johnson and a relief defendant, according to the complaint. About $40 million ended up on three platforms where some of it was used to trade other crypto assets, but little to no money was used to trade FX. After October 2025, the scheme raised about $350 million, and none of it was sent to Coinbase. Where the money went The SEC said the defendants made more than $250 million in Ponzi payments to earlier investors and moved more than $220 million to themselves. The money paid for exotic cars, expensive homes, private air travel and other businesses they owned, and helped feed Johnson’s gambling. Promoters took more than $50 million. Anderson is accused of producing fake financial reports, including at least two “audit reports” and a “quality of earnings” report from a supposedly independent firm. The SEC said the documents falsely claimed the returns had been verified against bank and brokerage records. It said Anderson did no audit work, was not independent and had a financial stake in the scheme. entertainment.title: Asali Africa: Serves Up ‘There’s Rice at Home’ A New Cooking Series Hosted by Chef Soliat Bada
entertainment.description: Chef Soliat Bada Anyone who grew up in a Nigerian home knows the line. You suggest buying food outside, and before you finish the sentence, someone reminds you that there’s rice at home. It is usually the end of the conversation. In Asali Africa’s new series, it is where the conversation starts. There’s Rice at Home is a cooking and conversation show from Asali Africa, the Lagos-based creative development agency, hosted by Chef Soliat Bada . In each episode, Soliat cooks one rice dish with a guest, and while the pot does its work, the two get into the kind of talk that usually happens around food: family, money and what success really looks like. Rice is the most ordinary thing in a Nigerian kitchen, and the show makes a good case that it doesn’t have to taste ordinary. Over five episodes, released every two weeks, the menu travels from Jamaica to Saudi Arabia, back home to Nigeria and on to Louisiana. You don’t just watch the food get made, either. The recipes are written up in full on Asali Africa’s website, with the ingredients and method laid out step by step, so you can watch Soliat cook a dish and then make it in your own kitchen. The season opens with Rice and Peas with Oxtail, the Jamaican Sunday staple of rice cooked in coconut milk with red kidney beans (the “peas”), served beside rich, slow-cooked oxtail. Soliat’s guest is Michael Famoroti , co-founder of Stears, and their conversation turns to family and black tax: the expectation that once you start earning, you start supporting the people who raised you. entertainment.title: Lagos Hosts 2026 International Theatre Festival, Featuring Local and International Productions
entertainment.description: The third edition of the Lagos International Theatre Festival (LITF) has concluded successfully, attracting over 20,000 attendees from November 9 to 15, 2026. Featuring more than 25 productions, international performances from Kenya, Brazil, Norway and Canada, high-profile diplomatic engagements and a spectacular Opening Night Gala, the festival reinforced its growing position as an important platform for showcasing Nigerian creativity and connecting global theatre communities. The impressive turnout, diversity of productions and international participation demonstrated the growing appetite for live theatre and the potential of cultural platforms to stimulate creative enterprise, encourage international collaboration and strengthen Nigeria’s global cultural presence. A Vision For Global Recognition Speaking on the success of the festival, Founder and Creative Producer, Bolanle Austen-Peters , said: “Our ambition has always been to create more than a theatre festival. We want to build a platform that places Lagos firmly on the global cultural map, gives African stories the international visibility they deserve and creates meaningful opportunities for our artists. Welcoming over 20,000 attendees, presenting more than 25 productions and bringing international performers from four countries to Lagos is a powerful affirmation of this vision. Theatre is not just entertainment; it is an instrument of cultural identity, economic opportunity and global influence. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. entertainment.title: Visa Report Identifies Opportunity to Integrate Digital Payments with SMEs Business Operations in Nigeria
entertainment.description: Report identifies next SME digitization opportunity: connecting payments with day-to-day business management. 94% of SMEs surveyed find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, yet only 29% currently use one, pointing to untapped demand for tools that connect payments with business management. Integrated payment and business solutions can give financial institutions a more holistic view of SME cash flow and support more tailored financing solutions over time. Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria have largely moved beyond the first stage of digital payment adoption, but a productivity gap remains. According to Visa’s new survey for its Pay and Get Paid 2026 report, most of the SMEs surveyed in Nigeria use digital payments, showing how firmly digital commerce has taken root in the country’s small business economy. However, many SMEs still manage the related financial and operational tasks separately, with only 29% currently using an integrated solution that connects payments with broader business management. The report shows that financial admin and disconnected tools create friction for SMEs, with surveyed businesses citing challenges in tracking outstanding invoices (14%), keeping payroll records organized (19%), and preparing financial reports (16%). These pain points reflect a disconnect between payments and the operational tasks that follow, with some businesses juggling multiple systems to keep their business running. The appetite for a more connected approach is clear. According to the report, 94% of SMEs find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, reflecting strong interest in tools that can bring payments and key business operations into one experience. However, adoption has yet to catch up: only 29% of SMEs currently use an integrated payment and business platform. The report points to several perception barriers that may be slowing adoption. Businesses cited that they already have manual processes that work (8%), that an integrated platform may disrupt their current way of working (8%), or that they do not trust relying on a single provider (7%). These findings suggest that broader adoption will depend on helping SMEs better understand how integrated tools can be relevant, accessible, and scalable for businesses at different stages of growth. At the same time, the experience of SMEs already using integrated solutions suggests a strong value case. The report found that Nigerian businesses using an integrated tool or platform report 93% satisfaction, with 88% reporting efficiency gains, including reductions in the time and effort required to manage their business. Beyond efficiency, integrated platforms may also create new opportunities for financial institutions to deepen SME relationships by using richer payments and business-management data to better understand cash flow patterns, support risk assessment, and potentially enable more relevant lending solutions over time. entertainment.description: Sade Adu in the Performer category and Fela Kuti in the Early Influence category, both inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Class of 2026. Nigerian music history just added another major chapter in Los Angeles, and the celebration has been loud from Lagos to London. On Saturday, 14 November 2026, Afrobeat pioneer Fela Aníkúlápó Kuti and Nigerian-British singer Sade Adu were officially inducted into the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame during a star-studded ceremony at the Peacock Theatre. For Fela Kuti, nearly three decades after his passing in 1997, this induction makes him the first African-born solo artist to enter the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame. Honoured posthumously in the Early Influence category—five years after he was first nominated in 2021—the recognition celebrates how he fused West African rhythms with jazz, funk, and soul to create Afrobeat, using his voice and horns to confront social and political injustice across classics like “Zombie”, “Water No Get Enemy”, and “Sorrow, Tears and Blood”. It also caps off an extraordinary 2026 for his legacy, coming just months after the Recording Academy presented him with a posthumous Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award in February, another first for an African artist. Speaking on the milestone, the family reflected on how remarkable it is to see Fela receive both the Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award and a Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction in the very same year. Meanwhile, Sade Adu —born Helen Folasade Adu in Ibadan—was inducted in th e Performer category as the frontwoman of her acclaimed British band Sade , alongside longtime bandmates Stuart Matthewman , Paul Spencer Denman , and Andrew Hale . Earning their spot on their second nomination, the group behind timeless soul-jazz records such as “Smooth Operator”, “The Sweetest Taboo”, and “Your Love Is King” opted to sit out the ceremony in true low-key fashion, though they shared a warm message thanking fans and dedicating the milestone to their late longtime producer Mike Pela . (is associated with: «Bayern don't rule out Musiala sale as Rummenigge escalates dilemma») Tom Weller/dpa Bayern Munich are not ruling out the sale of Jamal Musiala as fresh statements from supervisory board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge have escalated the situation surrounding the midfielder. Musiala has been struggling with fitness since a serious injury at last year's Club World Cup, which forced him to miss half of the 2025-26 season. He made his comeback from yet another injury in Bayern's 1-1 draw with Cologne in the Bundesliga on Friday evening. However, there are concerns over his health after he collapsed earlier this year during two pre-season games. He later went public about a neurological condition. "He has a health-related issue. It's also well known that he has a contract involving very substantial sums of money. As a club, we have to consider how to deal with that situation. I think that's responsible and perfectly normal," Rummenigge said after the draw with Cologne. He said that selling the player "it's not out of the question. We suspect it will be difficult for him to get back to his previous level." However, Rummenigge added that he can't imagine another club would buy Musiala "under these circumstances. We have to think about the financial implications." Bayern honorary president Uli Hoeness recently has also expressed doubts whether Musiala would ever return to his previous level of play. "He has an illness that is not easily curable, but can be controlled to some extent with medication. But whether he will ever again have the performance level he once had..." "But now he is still getting paid. Just imagine if Bayern were now to question his contract and say: what he can now deliver is no longer what was in the contract," he said referring to Musiala's deal until 2030. Hoeness was criticized for his statements, but Rummenigge backed the remarks. "Uli's wording was correct. Very serious and fair. We have an interest in seeing him return and play well. sports.description: The Buffalo Bills are looking to stay in the win column in Week 11 as they head back home to take on the Miami Dolphins at Highmark Stadium. The Bills (8-1) have won their last five games and are trying to keep the momentum going. How can Buffalo get the upper hand against the Dolphins (1-8)? Here are Bills Wire's three keys to victory in Week 11: Efficient passing Last week against the New York Jets, Josh Allen completed just 52.4% of his passes (11-for-21), recorded a passer rating of 80.7, and threw an interception. While Allen scored twice with his legs and the Bills ran away with the game, it wasn't an efficient game from him. This week, he'll have a chance to bounce back against another divisional rival. This year, the Dolphins are allowing the highest completion percentage for opposing quarterbacks in the NFL (73.7%). Allen and the passing game have a chance to get right at an important part of the season. Work the ground game James Cook continues to be the workhorse for the Bills offense, having at least 18 carries in seven of the last eight games for Buffalo. Last week, he ran for 157 yards and a touchdown, including a 74-yard house call to put the Jets to bed. The Dolphins have struggled on defense this year. They have the 27th-ranked run defense according to DVOA. The Bills should look to take control of this one and pound the rock. Perhaps they'll look to involve Ray Davis more out of the backfield in this one with a short week coming up for the Chiefs Thanksgiving matchup. Keep beating up on backup QBs The Bills defense has caught a break recently. Over their last three games, the've faced a backup QB in every matchup due to injury. In Week 8, they faced both Tyley Huntley and Joe Fagnano of the Ravens after Lamar Jackson went down. In Week 9 against the Vikings, they faced Carson Wentz. And, in Week 10, Geno Smith exited and they faced rookie Cade Clubnik. The Bills defense has stepped up in a major way the past three weeks after a rocky start to the season. They didn't allow a single touchdown in all three games. But, how much of it is from facing low-level offenses and how much should be credited to the defense for turning things around? It is more of the same for the Bills this week as they'll get Dolphins rookie QB Kyle McCord out of Syracuse after Malik Willis was put on IR . sports.description: The Michigan Wolverines are reportedly making another change at quarterback, and this time, Bryce Underwood is getting the call. With Michigan preparing to host undefeated UCLA on Saturday afternoon, head coach Kyle Whittingham is expected to turn back to the sophomore quarterback who began the season as the team’s starter. According to Pete Nakos of On3 , Underwood is expected to start against the Bruins, replacing freshman Tommy Carr, who has started Michigan’s previous four games. The decision comes at a critical time for the Wolverines, who enter Saturday’s matchup with a 5-5 record and need one more victory to become bowl eligible. Michigan has struggled to find consistency at quarterback throughout the 2026 season, and the latest reported change suggests the coaching staff is still searching for answers. With the fourth-ranked Bruins coming to Ann Arbor, Underwood is about to get another opportunity to prove he can lead Michigan’s struggling offense. sports.title: Browns roster: 2 backups who could help take the offense to another level
sports.description: Fans of the Cleveland Browns are enjoying a peaceful bye week before preparing for Week 12’s Sunday Night Football matchup with the Las Vegas Raiders . There are still a ton of questions surrounding the Browns, including whether they are actually a good team or just happened to win games . Cleveland HC Todd Monken must use the bye week to get the team’s running game going and figure out how to help in the early part of the game . Beyond that, the offense has to find more stabilit y, much of which could come through the rushing attack and a schedule with defenses that can be attacked . While many will point to the offensive line, QB Deshaun Watson , and RB Quinshon Judkins as places where the Browns offense needs to improve, two backups could help take the offense to another level: RB Dylan Sampson and WR Isaiah Bond . Now, neither player is likely to take over significantly more snaps for the rest of the season, although Bond needs a few more if he’s going to make any impact at all, but both have a chance to help Monken’s offense be more explosive in different ways. Sampson is not just a change-of-pace back, but one who can make big plays in ways that Judkins just can’t. Misdirection runs, screen plays, dump-off passes, and the occasional late leak-out play could all give Watson and company big gains and keep the offense on the field. Sampson’s ability to make plays all over the field and from a variety of positions makes him a versatile threat that must be accounted for. Bond, on the other hand, has really one gift to give the Browns offense: straight-line speed. Unfortunately, mistimed jumps and drops have led Monken to limit the speedster’s snaps in favor of veterans Malachi Corley and Tylan Wallace . It also doesn’t help Bond’s chances that the top three receivers, KC Concepcion, Denzel Boston , and Jerry Jeudy , have deep route speed and ability, but Bond speed is unique. If Monken can trust the second-year receiver and he makes just a couple of big plays in the first few games coming out of the bye week, Bond can not only become impactful in the stat sheet but also as a decoy. Having Bond run deep post, 9-route, and corner routes can take the top off of a defense, pull the safety away, and create more spacing underneath for all of the above-mentioned players, along with TE Harold Fannin Jr. , to make plays after the catch. Cleveland’s offense will not be decided by the performances of Sampson and Bond, but both backups have a chance to take the unit’s performance to another level, assuming that the line, QB play, and starting weapons are doing as well as or better than they have so far this season. Barring injury, neither is likely to be a fantasy star or steal significant snaps from any starters, but their impact with explosive plays could move things from good to great. sports.title: Incredible number of Newcastle United v Arsenal tickets still on sale on Saturday afternoon
sports.description: Jacob Murphy Newcastle United v Arsenal I thought I would have a look just in case, see if by chance any Newcastle United v Arsenal tickets were available on Saturday afternoon. Just in case you aren’t aware, the club allow Newcastle United season ticket holders to sell their tickets for individual Premier League games. This was a very positive move by the club as it means that seats don’t need to be left empty if a season ticket holder is ill for example. Using the online club system, season ticket holders can make their ticket available for a league match, with Newcastle United members then able to go onto the NUFC official ticketing site (you have to be then logged in as a member to see the tickets that are available) to buy. The club also make money from this. As I understand it, the fan (season ticket holder) selling the ticket is credited with the pro rata match price of their season ticket and if the ticket is then bought by a member, they are charged the far higher single ticket price, with the club banking the difference. As a member, I had no luck in the ballot for Newcastle United v Arsenal tickets. The same when it came to the queue sale. The demand was huge, I had a ridiculously high number for the queue sale and stood no chance, along with countless thousands of other Newcastle United members. Anyway, I have just went onto the club’s ticketing site (just before 2pm on Saturday) and I couldn’t believe how many Newcastle United v Arsenal tickets were on sale! To be honest, I wasn’t expecting there to be any, I was just looking in the vain hope I might hit very lucky. What I found was I had a choice of all around St James’ Park ! All four stands with plenty tickets up for sale from season ticket holders. I snapped up a couple for me and my mate for the East Stand and after sending this article into The Mag I will be heading off to the Toon to meet up with the lads (mostly season ticket holders) for some pre-match refreshments. After buying our tickets I counted up all the Newcastle United v Arsenal tickets that season ticket holders are trying to sell and there were 147 available (it had been 149 I guess before I snapped up ours). Apologies for my wonky photography skills but the red areas are where there were Newcastle United v Arsenal tickets available just over three and a half hours before the match… Newcastle United v Arsenal tickets I am over the moon getting these tickets but at the same time absolutely stunned that so many season ticket holders are trying to flog their tickets. Is it because they think Arsenal will win? Is it because it is a bit chilly? Is it because they will get too upset seeing Bruno Guimaraes in an Arsenal shirt? Anyway, if you are a member who didn’t get a ticket for today’s match, log onto the official ticketing site and take your pick!!

Explaining the club’s plans, Perez said : “We have already taken the first major step. sports.title: Match Report And Player Ratings: Manchester City 1-1 Fulham (Premier League)
sports.description: Match Report And Player Ratings: Manchester City 1-1 Fulham (Premier League) It was another dreary first-half from Enzo Maresca’s side, with Fulham causing all manner of problems and taking the lead through Rodrigo Muniz. The Blues were reinvigorated in the second-half and equalised through Elliot Anderson, but didn’t do enough to push on for a winner and thus were left with another poor result. Fulham’s high press was severely disrupting Manchester City ’s attempts to play out from the back in the early exchanges, but some inroads were made and the Blues generated the game’s first half-chances, Erling Haaland’s shot blocked by David Affengruber and Nico O’Reilly seeing an effort deflect into the side netting. But for the fourth Premier League game in a row, City fell behind inside the opening 20 minutes. Ex-Blue Oscar Bobb escaped the attentions of Elliot Anderson and fed Muniz, who deceived Abdukodir Khusanov and stuck the ball into Gianluigi Donnarumma’s top corner to deepen Maresca’s concerns. City thought they had had their equaliser soon after when Iliman Ndiaye’s cross found Haaland and his initial shot was fumbled by Bernd Leno, allowing the Norwegian to follow up, but the referee deemed that the goalkeeper had two hands on it at the time of the striker’s second kick, meaning a foul and no goal. Fulham almost took advantage of that reprieve to double their lead, Bobb again leading a breakaway and only Ruben Dias’ late intervention clearing Josh King’s dangerous low cross. It was a pitiful first half-hour and Manchester City fans inside the Etihad Stadium began booing and jeering at the players’ unwillingness to press high and take the ball off of a Fulham side meandering around in their own half. City won the ball, Phil Foden found Haaland in behind and he blazed over a massive chance. City’s pace had finally improved, and Elliot Anderson succeeded in breaking through the lines to find Nico O’Reilly in a crossing position, but Haaland was again wayward, this time via a deflection. Ruben Dias put a free header over from the resulting corner. Despite that pressure, City were lucky not to go 2-0 down on the brink of the break. O’Reilly switched off in the box and it broke for Bobb, who was denied a goal on his return to the Etihad by a big Donnarumma save. At the other end, the final action of the half was an incredibly weak shot from Jeremy Doku into Leno’s arms. Manchester City needed a bolt of inspiration from somewhere, and Anderson provided it. A Foden corner was cleared to the edge, and the midfield man was on the scene with a fantastic drilled volley, which flew below the radar of Leno and in. And it was nearly two for the summer signing just after the hour, as he darted onto a Haaland offering and nearly squeezed his effort past Leno, the ball rolling narrowly wide. sports.description: New York Giants defensive back Jevon Holland and Deonte Banks celebrate after an interception. | Getty Images There were, if not outright concerns, certainly questions about how good the New York Giants defense could be in 2026. Between edge defenders Brian Burns, Abdul Carter, and Kayvon Thibodeaux, as well as off-ball linebackers Tremaine Edmunds, Arvell Reese, and Micah McFadden, the Giants’ linebacking corps was expected to be one of the best in the NFL. And the hope was that their defensive line would at least be serviceable after the addition of veteran defensive tackles D.J. Reader and Shelby Harris. The bigger questions were about the Giants’ secondary, particularly after Cor’Dale Flott left in free agency. 2025 free agents Paulson Adebo and Jevon Holland hadn’t panned out in their first years as Giants, while 2023 first round pick Deonte Banks had regressed badly under DC Shane Bowen and was considered a bust. The Giants signed former Cleveland Browns and Jacksonville Jaguars cornerback Greg Newsome II, as well as former Baltimore Ravens safety Ar’Darius Washington, in the 2026 free agency period and drafted Tennessee cornerback Colton Hood in the second round of the draft. However, those moves weren’t viewed as much more than Band-Aids for a Giants’ secondary, and national commentors suggested that the Giants’ scondary could be putrid in the first year of John Harbaugh’s rebuild.
